subsystems.name: Reflector and active surface
subsystems.role: a 500 m dish that reshapes itself to keep a parabola focused as it tracks.
parts: motorised actuators at the net nodes

subsystems.name: Feed cabin and positioning
subsystems.role: suspends the receiver at the focus and steers it around the sky.
parts: focus cabin with receivers and amplifiers

subsystems.name: Receivers
subsystems.role: convert radio waves to electrical signals with the lowest possible noise.
parts: ultra-wideband receiver covering a few hundred MHz to about 1.6 GHz

subsystems.name: Timing and signal chain
subsystems.role: digitises wide bands while keeping absolute time, which is what reveals a drifting signal.
parts: optical fibre links to the control room

subsystems.name: Search computing
subsystems.role: sifts terabytes for the rare narrow channel that behaves like a transmitter.

subsystems.name: RFI monitoring and protection
subsystems.role: keeps Earth-made signals from drowning the search.

buildSteps.title: Choose the site
buildSteps.detail: A natural karst bowl in Guizhou, deep enough to hold the dish and shielded from much of the surrounding radio traffic.

buildSteps.title: Design the cable net
buildSteps.detail: Structural modelling works out a net whose nodes can be pulled to form a small parabola inside the large sphere.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the panels
buildSteps.detail: Thousands of aluminium triangles are made and mounted on the net, each tied to actuators below.

buildSteps.title: Rig the feed cabin
buildSteps.detail: Winches and cables are installed so the focus cabin can be held and moved above the dish.

buildSteps.title: Install receivers and backends
buildSteps.detail: Multibeam feeds, cryogenic amplifiers, digitisers and fibre links are fitted and calibrated.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate the surface
buildSteps.detail: The dish shape is measured and corrected until the focused beam is good enough for faint-signal work.

buildSteps.title: Observe
buildSteps.detail: Targets are tracked, or the sky drifts past, while the whole band is recorded for later search.

buildSteps.title: Search and veto
buildSteps.detail: Coherent dedispersion and drift searches pull out narrowband candidates, which are tested against interference by re-observing and by changing pointing.

buildSteps.title: Confirm
buildSteps.detail: Only a signal that repeats, moves with the sky and survives every interference test becomes a serious candidate.

prerequisites.why: a fixed sphere cannot focus; the surface must deform continuously to track a source.
system noise sets how faint a transmitter can be seen, and beams set how much sky each pointing covers.
gigabits per second of raw voltage have to be dedispersed and searched faster than they arrive.

prerequisites.tech: A radio-quiet site with interference mitigation
prerequisites.why: even in a protected valley, satellites, aircraft and ground transmitters produce narrowband signals that mimic the target.
a single dish cannot prove a signal is not local; other telescopes in other countries must see it too.

pathway.milestone: targeted searches of nearby stars and their exoplanets, plus commensal searching of data recorded for pulsar and fast-radio-burst surveys
pathway.unlocks: the deepest narrowband limits available on any single dish, over the sky it can see

pathway.milestone: better interference rejection and automatic follow-up, so candidates can be checked within minutes
pathway.unlocks: far fewer false alarms from satellites and phones

pathway.milestone: coordinated observing with interferometer arrays in the southern hemisphere
pathway.unlocks: sky coverage and direction-finding that a single dish cannot provide
the ability to scan large areas of sky, not just point at chosen stars

pathway.milestone: an agreed international verification and announcement procedure if a signal survives every test
pathway.unlocks: a credible, checkable claim rather than a headline
